subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded, WASM, C, or Rust ports, or should projects like MimiClaw remain independent ports without an OpenClaw compatibility contract?
rationale: This choice affects core runtime ownership, plugin SDK boundaries, provider/auth selection, storage/session semantics, tool execution, streaming events, and security policy, so it cannot be safely resolved as a cleanup close or autonomous fix PR.

options.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
options.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and owner boundary before accepting any no-Node or embedded implementation.

options.title: Scope To Plugin SDK Only
options.body: Route near-term non-TypeScript work through plugin or JSON-RPC harness APIs while explicitly leaving no-Node agent ports outside the supported OpenClaw runtime contract.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Declare OpenClaw a Node-hosted product for now and treat MimiClaw-style ports as independent projects without compatibility promises.

recommendation.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and owner boundary before accepting any no-Node or embedded implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current and historical signals for runtime guard, harness docs, and prior issue review route through steipete.
